The sole ordinary implementation association in spec.rs is supported by parse_anchors finishing the active anchor at source.len(), finish_anchor taking only that bounded slice, and load_workspace/add_chapter_text parsing each dedented prose block separately with local state and remapped offsets. Markdown documents likewise receive separate parse calls.

All three ordinary test entries supply meaningful assertions. claims_retain_all_blocks_until_the_next_definition_or_document_end checks the last anchor's exact final qualification and source slice through document end, including trailing whitespace trimming. sage_prose_rules_have_precise_spans_model_owners_and_cross_source_references checks exact value and member contents across adjacent prose blocks and exact query content/span before envelope syntax; these assertions reject leakage across blocks, declarations or method bodies. Its value content and original span also preserve multiline Unicode prose and indentation while excluding delimiters. an_end_marker_in_another_sage_prose_block_is_unmatched checks the first block's exact bounded content and a single correctly located no-active-anchor error for a marker in the following block, detecting state crossing the block boundary. Captured source() and BookFixture helpers confirm these assertions consume real SpecIndex parsing. There are no TODO/N/A entries or deferred prerequisites.

Baseline verification: independently compared current files with the historical input. spec.rs is an exact byte match. The only test-file delta changes review claim access to the new Claim fragment selector; expected content and boundary assertions remain unchanged. This preserves the historical rationale, independently reassessed above. Initial fragments plus recorded helper reads cover dependencies used for this assessment.
